source.patents: U.S. Bureau of Land Management, General Land Office Records (glorecords.blm.gov), land patents for Townships 18 and 19 South, Range 8 East, Salt Lake Meridian, Emery County, Utah, 1883 to 1920. Each row links to its record.
source.geometry: BLM National Public Land Survey System (CadNSDI), PLSS Intersected layer. Each quarter-quarter section or government lot named in a legal description was looked up and the pieces of one patent joined. No parcel was drawn by hand.
source.scope: A federal patent records the day title first passed from the United States. It is not a record of later sales, and it does not show who owned the land in any later year. The platted town of Castle Dale lies almost wholly on land patented to individuals between 1884 and 1903; the transfer of town lots to householders is a matter for county deed records and is not part of this table.
source.reading: Every patent that has an image was read from the image, not only from the index. The kind of entry follows the patent itself: 17 patents the index calls cash sales are Desert Land final certificates. Names follow the index spelling. One legal description (no. 117) is taken from the image because the index leaves it blank.
source.citationFull: U.S. Bureau of Land Management, “General Land Office Records,” database with images (https://glorecords.blm.gov : accessed October 2026), land patents, Salt Lake City land office, T18S and T19S R8E, Salt Lake Meridian; compiled as the Castle Dale One Place Study land register, Encyclopedia of Emery County.
